# Tracks { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks(chroms=None, *, assembly=None, **kw)
```

WebGL2 genomic segment viewer rendered as a Jupyter widget.

Build a stack of tracks by chaining the ``add_*_track`` methods, then
display the instance directly in a notebook cell. All pan / zoom is
uniform-only (zero CPU/GPU buffer work per frame); segment viewport
culling uses sorted attribute-pointer offsets.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**chroms**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to int, or str]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Chromosome sizes as a ``{chrom: length}`` mapping, or an assembly name such as ``'hg38'``. The first chromosome is shown initially.

<code>[**assembly**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Assembly name (``'hg38'``, ``'rheMac10'``, …) whose chromosome sizes are looked up with :func:`geneinfo.coords.chromosome_lengths`; an alternative to ``chroms``. Give one of ``chroms`` and ``assembly``, not both. The assembly is also the default for :meth:`add_gene_track`.

<code>[****kw**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [{}]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Passed on to :class:`anywidget.AnyWidget`; ``theme=`` overrides the default theme (see :func:`set_default_theme`).

## Track types {.doc-section .doc-section-track-types}

:meth:`add_segment_track`
    Instanced GPU rectangles with automatic level-of-detail (LOD)
    density fallback when zoomed out.
:meth:`add_heatmap_track`
    R8 texture rendering; handles 10 k+ individuals at 60 fps.
:meth:`add_gene_track`
    Exon blocks plus intron connectors (drawn on the 2D overlay).
:meth:`add_point_track`
    Point cloud (``gl.POINTS``).
:meth:`add_line_track`
    Connected polyline per group (``gl.LINE_STRIP``).
:meth:`add_fill_track`
    Fill-between two curves with optional pos/neg colour split.
:meth:`add_histogram_track`
    Vertical bars with multi-resolution LOD.
:meth:`add_arc_track`
    Arcs linking pairs of genomic positions.
:meth:`add_ucsc_track`
    A UCSC Genome Browser track fetched by name and drawn as a point,
    line, histogram, fill, segment or heatmap track.

Point and line tracks accept ``y_scale='log'`` for a base-10 log
y-axis.

## Toolbar {.doc-section .doc-section-toolbar}

The widget renders a single-row toolbar above the canvas:

Chromosome dropdown
    Switches the visible chromosome and resets the viewport to the
    full chromosome span.
Position box
    Free-text region selector. Accepts ``chr1:1,000–2,000`` or
    ``chr1:1000-2000`` (the chromosome prefix is optional and
    defaults to the current one). Press ``Enter`` to jump.
``＋``  *Zoom in*
    Halves the visible window around its centre.
``－``  *Zoom out*
    Doubles the visible window around its centre (clamped to the
    chromosome).
``⌂``  *Reset view*
    Restores the viewport to the full chromosome (or, when a
    heatmap defines a tighter pan range, that range).
``⟲``  *Recompute heatmap(s)*
    Visible only when at least one heatmap track is present.
    Re-bins every heatmap at the current viewport for higher
    resolution. Routed through the ``_cmd_heatmap_recompute``
    command to :meth:`_rebin_heatmap_for_view`.
``◱``  *Restore global heatmap*
    Visible only when at least one heatmap track is present.
    Restores the original whole-chromosome heatmap pixels via
    :meth:`_restore_heatmap_global`.
``⧉``  *Snapshot*
    Composites the WebGL and overlay canvases and writes a PNG to
    the system clipboard (falls back to a file download when
    clipboard access is denied). The button briefly flashes ``✓``
    on success or ``!`` on failure.
LOD badge
    Read-only indicator showing the current segment-track render
    mode: ``▬ segments`` when individual rectangles are drawn,
    ``▒ density`` when the density LOD is active.

## Pan and zoom {.doc-section .doc-section-pan-and-zoom}

Mouse wheel
    Scroll wheel zooms in/out anchored on the cursor's genomic
    position. The zoom-step factor per wheel tick is
    :attr:`zoom_speed`.
Click-drag
    Press and drag inside the plot area to pan along the
    chromosome.
Double-click
    Halves the visible window around the click position (a faster
    alternative to the ``＋`` button when targeting a specific
    location).
Keyboard (when the widget has focus or hover)
    ``←`` / ``→`` pan by 15 % of the current window.
    ``+`` / ``=`` zoom in by 1.5×; ``-`` zooms out by 1.5×.
Tooltip
    Hovering over a track displays a tooltip whose contents come
    from the track's ``tip_fmt`` / ``tip_label``. The tooltip
    disappears on ``mouseleave``.

## Synchronised attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-synchronised-attributes}

These traits round-trip between Python and the browser; assigning
them from Python updates the rendered view immediately.

chrom_sizes : dict of str to int
    Chromosome name → length in base pairs. Set once via
    :meth:`__init__`; re-assigning it rebuilds the dropdown and
    the pan-clamp ranges.
track_configs : list of dict
    One config per track. Maintained by the ``add_*_track``
    methods and :meth:`remove_track` / :meth:`clear_tracks`; do
    not mutate directly.
track_data : dict
    Track-id-keyed payloads consumed by the JS uploader. Maintained
    by the ``add_*_track`` methods and :meth:`remove_track` /
    :meth:`clear_tracks`; do not mutate directly.
viewport : dict
    ``{'chrom': str, 'start': int, 'end': int}``. Use
    :meth:`set_viewport` or :meth:`zoom_to` to change it from
    Python; the JS side updates it in response to pan/zoom and
    toolbar input.
zoom_speed : float, default ``1.02``
    Multiplicative zoom step per wheel-tick. Higher values zoom
    faster.
pan_speed : float, default ``1.0``
    Multiplier for click-drag pan velocity (genomic units per CSS
    pixel of mouse movement).
min_span : int, default ``500``
    Narrowest viewport width in base pairs — the point past which
    zooming in stops. Applies to the wheel, double-click and the
    ``+`` key alike. Lower it to inspect individual bases (e.g.
    ``min_span=100``); it is clamped to the chromosome's own span, so
    a value larger than the chromosome cannot lock the view.
theme : dict
    Colour palette and layout knobs. See :data:`DARK_THEME` and
    :data:`LIGHT_THEME` for the recognised keys; numeric values
    like ``sidebar_w`` (CSS pixel width of the left label column)
    live alongside the colour strings. Mutating the trait via
    ``viewer.theme = {...}`` re-applies the theme without reload.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> viewer = Tracks(chrom_sizes={'chr1': 248_956_422})
>>> (viewer
...  .add_gene_track(assembly='hg38')
...  .zoom_to('chr1', 50_000_000, window=10_000_000))
>>> viewer  # display in a notebook cell
```

### add_arc_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_arc_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_arc_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    pos1='pos1',
    pos2='pos2',
    group_by=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    height=None,
    arc_height=None,
    alpha=0.9,
    line_width=1.5,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
)
```

Add an arc track connecting pairs of positions on the same chromosome.

Each record is drawn as a quadratic-Bezier curve from ``pos1`` to
``pos2`` with a fixed apex height above the track baseline, clamped
so the apex never leaves the track band. Useful for splice
junctions, Hi-C interactions, structural-variant links, and
similar pairwise-coordinate data.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, ``pos1``, ``pos2`` (names configurable via ``pos1`` / ``pos2``) and the optional ``group_by`` column.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**pos1**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'pos1\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column names for the two endpoints. Order within a row doesn't matter — the track normalises to ``(min, max)``.

<code>[**pos2**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'pos1\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column names for the two endpoints. Order within a row doesn't matter — the track normalises to ``(min, max)``.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose unique values become separately-coloured arc groups. When omitted, all arcs share a single colour.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. Omitted means the palette cycle supplies one colour per group.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [str, list, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Qualitative palette; used only when ``color_map`` isn't given.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Total track height in CSS pixels. When omitted it is derived from ``arc_height`` (``arc_height + 6``) so the band fits the arcs; if both are omitted the track defaults to 60.

<code>[**arc_height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Apex height above the baseline in CSS pixels — how tall the arcs are drawn. When omitted it fills the usable band (``height - 6``, where 6 = ``2 * PAD_V``). If both ``height`` and ``arc_height`` are given and the apex would overflow the band, ``arc_height`` is clamped to ``height - 6`` (with a warning) so the arcs never leave the track.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [0.9]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Line opacity (0..1).

<code>[**line_width**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [1.5]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Stroke width in CSS pixels.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{group}``, ``{pos1}``, ``{pos2}``, ``{span}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

### add_fill_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_fill_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_fill_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    x='pos',
    y=None,
    y_lo=None,
    y_hi=None,
    group_by=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    color_pos='C0',
    color_neg='C3',
    alpha=1.0,
    height=60,
    y_range=None,
    baseline=None,
    step=None,
    zoom_windows=(256, 1024, 4096),
    aggregate='envelope',
    y_range_per_zoom=True,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
    density_windows=None,
    y_range_per_lod=None,
)
```

Add a fill-between track.

Either supply ``y`` (fill from a single curve to ``baseline``) or
both ``y_lo`` and ``y_hi`` (fill between two curves). When
``baseline`` is set, the area above and below it can be drawn in
distinct colours.

A missing value (``NaN`` in ``y``, or in either ``y_lo`` or
``y_hi``) breaks the fill, as in matplotlib: nothing is filled
between the samples on either side of it. Positions that simply
have no row are bridged, so add ``NaN`` rows where the fill should
break. When zoomed out, a bin whose samples are all ``NaN`` is a
gap; other bins aggregate their non-``NaN`` samples.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, the column named by ``x``, plus the relevant y column(s).

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**x**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'pos\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for genomic position.

<code>[**y**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for a single curve; the fill runs between it and ``baseline`` (``0`` unless you move it). An alias for ``y_hi``, accepted whenever ``y_lo`` is not passed — pass one spelling or the other, never both.

<code>[**y_lo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for the lower y boundary. Given without ``y_hi`` it is the single curve instead, and the *upper* edge of the fill is ``baseline`` (``0`` by default).

<code>[**y_hi**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for the upper y boundary. Given without ``y_lo`` it is the single curve instead, and the *lower* edge of the fill is ``baseline`` (``0`` by default) — the same thing ``y`` does. With neither boundary nor ``y`` supplied, the columns ``'lo'`` and ``'hi'`` are used.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose unique values become separate groups, each drawn in a single colour from ``color_map`` / ``palette``. Works with a single curve (``y``) and with a two-curve band. Because the colour identifies the group, there is no positive / negative split: ``color_pos`` and ``color_neg`` are ignored, and the fill on both sides of ``baseline`` takes the group's colour.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. When omitted, group colours cycle through ``'C0'``..``'C9'``.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [None, str, list, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Group palette, used when ``color_map`` is omitted. ``None`` uses the active matplotlib ``axes.prop_cycle``. Strings are resolved as colormap names first (``'viridis'``, ``'tab10'``, ...) then fall back to single-colour literals.

<code>[**color_pos**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'C0\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Colour for the region above ``baseline``. Resolved with :func:`resolve_color`. Ignored when ``group_by`` is given.

<code>[**color_neg**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'C3\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Colour for the region below ``baseline``. Ignored when ``group_by`` is given.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``1.0``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Fill opacity in ``[0, 1]``, applied to every group. Values outside the range are clamped. Lower it to see overlapping groups through each other.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [60]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels.

<code>[**y_range**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of (float, float)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``(y_min, y_max)``. Auto-computed from data with 5% padding when omitted.

<code>[**baseline**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   The fill's other edge in single-curve mode, and the y value at which the positive / negative colour split occurs. Defaults to ``0`` whenever a single curve is given (as ``y``, ``y_hi``, or ``y_lo``). With both ``y_lo`` and ``y_hi`` it defaults to ``None``, which disables dual colouring. Pass an explicit number in lo/hi mode to re-enable the split. With ``group_by`` the split is always off and each group is drawn in its own colour.

<code>[**step**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Step mode for a staircase fill, matching matplotlib's ``fill_between(step=...)``. One of ``'pre'``, ``'post'``, ``'mid'``. ``None`` gives smooth linear interpolation.

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, tuple thereof, or False]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``(256, 1024, 4096)``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Level-of-detail resolutions. Each entry is either a bin *count* (``int``) or a physical bin *size* (``str`` such as ``'10kb'``); a bp size is resolved to a count per chromosome. The renderer draws the coarsest level whose bins still cover at least 2 CSS pixels and falls back to the raw samples once they are far enough apart, so a dense band stays responsive when zoomed out. Pass ``False`` (or ``()``) to disable LOD and always ship only the raw samples.

<code>[**aggregate**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'envelope\', \'mean\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'envelope\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   How samples sharing a bin are combined. ``'envelope'`` takes the ``min`` of the lower and the ``max`` of the upper boundary, so a coarse level never draws a narrower band than the data it summarises. ``'mean'`` averages each boundary, which smooths the band but can hide spikes. In single-``y`` mode the aggregate is applied to ``y`` before the split against ``baseline``.

<code>[**y_range_per_zoom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Emit a per-level ``(y_min, y_max)`` so the axis rescales when the renderer switches levels. Ignored when ``y_range`` is given explicitly.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{group}``, ``{lo}``, ``{hi}``, ``{x}``. Tooltips always report the raw samples, never the aggregated levels.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``zoom_windows`` and ``y_range_per_zoom``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

<code>[**y_range_per_lod**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``zoom_windows`` and ``y_range_per_zoom``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[TypeError](`TypeError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If both ``y`` and ``y_hi`` are supplied — they are two spellings of the same curve.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``y`` is combined with ``y_lo``, if ``step`` is not in ``{None, 'pre', 'post', 'mid'}``, or if ``aggregate`` is not in ``{'envelope', 'mean'}``.

### add_gene_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_gene_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_gene_track(
    genes_data=None,
    exons_df=None,
    *,
    assembly=None,
    name='Genes',
    color=None,
    height=None,
    collapse=True,
    label_padding=0,
    highlight=None,
    highlight_color=None,
    highlight_fill_color=None,
    highlight_spine_color=None,
    highlight_outline_color=None,
    highlight_label_color=None,
    highlight_halo_color=None,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
)
```

Add a gene / exon annotation track.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**genes_data**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`) or [pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Either a dict mapping chromosome to a list of ``(gene_name, chrom, start, end, strand, transcripts)`` tuples (as returned by ``geneinfo``), or a DataFrame with columns ``chrom``, ``start``, ``end``, ``name``, ``strand``. Mutually exclusive with ``assembly``; exactly one must be provided.

<code>[**exons_df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Frame with ``chrom``, ``gene_name``, ``start``, ``end``. Only used with the DataFrame form of ``genes_data``.

<code>[**assembly**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Assembly identifier (e.g. ``'hg38'``). When given, ``genes_data`` is fetched automatically via :func:`geneinfo.coords.gene_coords_region` for every chromosome in :func:`geneinfo.coords.chromosome_lengths`. Mutually exclusive with ``genes_data``. If the assembly was already supplied to :class:`Tracks` itself, it is inherited from there and passing it again here raises :class:`ValueError`.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'Genes\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track display label.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Exon block colour for non-highlighted genes (matplotlib colour spec). Falls back to ``theme['gene_exon']``.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels. Defaults to the required number of rows (positive strand above, negative below, each with sub-lanes on overlap).

<code>[**collapse**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, merge exons across all transcripts into a single union set. If False, each transcript becomes its own row.

<code>[**label_padding**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [0]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Extra room reserved around every gene for its label, **in kilobases** — ``200`` means 200 kb (200,000 bp), and fractions are allowed (``0.5`` is 500 bp) — when assigning rows. The room is split evenly on both sides, matching the label the renderer draws centred on the gene, so two neighbours are pushed onto separate rows exactly when the gap between them is smaller than ``label_padding``, whatever their strands. Modeled as an invisible margin around each gene: row packing, label centring and label collision all see the padded extent, while the spine, exons, arrows and tooltip range continue to reflect the gene's true bounds. ``0`` reproduces plain overlap-only packing.  Raising this does pull the zoom at which labels appear wider, since labels never collide across rows — but it buys that only by adding rows, and the exchange rate is poor: roughly 2-4x the rows per doubling of the labelled span. Rows need about 30 px each (an 11 px label band plus the exon and a gap), so a ``height`` of 300 affords only ~10 before label bands start overlapping their neighbours. Reaching chromosome-wide labels this way would take dozens to hundreds of rows, so treat it as a modest adjustment rather than a way to label a whole chromosome. It is also a fixed genomic distance chosen here, so it does not adapt as you zoom, and raising ``height`` alone does *not* help — height only adds vertical air between the rows packing already decided on.

<code>[**highlight**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of str or dict of str to list of str]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Either a list of gene names (treated as ``{'fill': [...]}``) or a dict mapping a property key to a list of gene names. Valid keys are ``'fill'``, ``'stroke'``, ``'outline'``, ``'color'``, ``'bold'``, ``'italic'``, ``'underline'``, ``'halo'``. A gene may appear under multiple keys; all applicable properties are applied independently.

<code>[**highlight_color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated alias for ``highlight_fill_color``. Retained for backward compatibility with the list form of ``highlight``.

<code>[**highlight_fill_color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Exon fill colour for ``'fill'`` highlights.

<code>[**highlight_spine_color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Backbone colour for ``'stroke'`` highlights.

<code>[**highlight_outline_color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Exon outline colour for ``'outline'`` highlights.

<code>[**highlight_label_color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Gene-name text colour for ``'color'`` highlights.

<code>[**highlight_halo_color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Halo rectangle colour (may include alpha) for ``'halo'`` highlights.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{name}``, ``{strand}``, ``{start}``, ``{end}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If neither or both of ``genes_data`` and ``assembly`` are given, or if ``highlight`` carries an unknown property key.

### add_heatmap_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_heatmap_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_heatmap_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    start='start',
    end='end',
    individual_col=None,
    group_by=None,
    sort_by=None,
    color_map=None,
    value_col=None,
    palette=None,
    vmin=None,
    vmax=None,
    height=None,
    zoom_windows=1000,
    alpha=0.5,
    shade=None,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
    group_col=None,
    windows=None,
    density_windows=None,
)
```

Add a heatmap track — one row per individual, GPU texture rendering.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, the interval start and end columns (see ``start`` / ``end``), and the columns named by ``individual_col`` / ``group_by`` when given.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**start**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``, ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Columns holding each interval's start and end coordinates.

<code>[**end**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``, ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Columns holding each interval's start and end coordinates.

<code>[**individual_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column identifying each haplotype / sample row. When omitted, each group (or the whole table, without ``group_by``) is drawn as a single row, e.g. for an annotation track, and ``shade`` defaults to ``'count'``.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for grouping individuals into coloured bands.

<code>[**sort_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column used to sort individuals within each group.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. When omitted, colours cycle through the built-in palette in group order. Only used in density mode (when ``value_col`` is ``None``).

<code>[**value_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose per-segment values drive colouring. When omitted, the track renders in density mode (overlapping segments accumulate alpha, tinted per group).

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [str, list, dict, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Palette used when ``value_col`` is given. A colormap name (``'viridis'``) or ``Colormap`` instance triggers continuous mode; a ``{category: colour}`` dict or list of colours triggers discrete mode (up to 255 categories). Ignored when ``value_col`` is ``None``. When ``value_col`` is given but ``palette`` is omitted, a default is auto-picked: ``'viridis'`` for numeric columns, the built-in categorical cycle otherwise.

<code>[**vmin**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Continuous-mode normalisation range; auto-inferred from ``df[value_col]`` when omitted. Ignored in discrete mode.

<code>[**vmax**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Continuous-mode normalisation range; auto-inferred from ``df[value_col]`` when omitted. Ignored in discrete mode.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels. Defaults to ``max(90, n_individuals)``, i.e. at least one pixel per row.

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, or tuple thereof]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [1000]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Finest x-resolution of the binning. An ``int`` is a fixed bin *count* covering the binned span. A ``str`` is a physical bin *size* in base pairs (``'10kb'``, ``'1.5Mb'``, ``'500'`` — units ``bp``/``kb``/``Mb``/``Gb``, bare number means bp); the bin count is then derived from the span as ``ceil(span / size)``. Because the heatmap rebins to the visible window (the ⟲ button), a bp size yields a constant bp-per-bin resolution that reaches its full fineness once you zoom in — at whole-chromosome zoom it is capped at 8192 bins (a GPU texture-width limit). A tuple is accepted for symmetry with the other track types; the heatmap renders a single resolution, so it uses the *finest* entry for the current span.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [0.5]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Per-segment opacity (matplotlib-style). Density mode with ``shade='alpha'`` only — each overlapping segment adds ``alpha`` to the cell shading, clamped at ``1.0``. Must lie in ``(0, 1]``.

<code>[**shade**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'alpha\', \'count\', \'log_count\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'alpha\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   How density mode (no ``value_col``) shades a cell. Defaults to ``'alpha'`` with ``individual_col`` and to ``'count'`` without it, where many records share each row. ``'alpha'`` adds ``alpha`` per overlapping segment, which suits one row per sample, where a few segments overlap a cell. ``'count'`` shades by the number of segments overlapping the cell, scaled so the busiest cell in the binned window (the chromosome, or the view after ⟲) is fully shaded; use it when many records share a row, e.g. a whole annotation track. ``'log_count'`` scales ``log(1 + count)`` instead, keeping sparse regions visible next to hotspots. In the count modes the tooltip reports the cell's segment count.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{group}``, ``{individual}``, ``{nInd}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

<code>[**group_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``group_by`` (``group_col``) and ``zoom_windows`` (``windows``, ``density_windows``). Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

<code>[**windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``group_by`` (``group_col``) and ``zoom_windows`` (``windows``, ``density_windows``). Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``group_by`` (``group_col``) and ``zoom_windows`` (``windows``, ``density_windows``). Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``alpha`` is not in ``(0, 1]``, if ``shade`` is unknown or not ``'alpha'`` together with ``value_col``, if ``palette`` is supplied without ``value_col``, if ``value_col`` is missing from ``df``, or if a discrete palette has more than 255 categories.

### add_histogram_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_histogram_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_histogram_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    x='pos',
    y='value',
    group_by=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    height=60,
    y_range=None,
    bin_width=None,
    stack=False,
    zoom_windows=(256, 1024, 4096),
    aggregate='mean',
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
    density_windows=None,
)
```

Add a histogram track — vertical bars centred on each ``x``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, the column named by ``x``, and the column named by ``y``.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**x**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'pos\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for genomic position (the bin centre).

<code>[**y**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'value\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for bar height.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose unique values become separate groups.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. Defaults to the built-in palette cycled in group order.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [None, str, list, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Group palette, used when ``color_map`` is omitted. ``None`` uses the active matplotlib ``axes.prop_cycle``. Strings are resolved as colormap names first (``'viridis'``, ``'tab10'``, ...) then fall back to single-colour literals.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [60]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels.

<code>[**y_range**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of (float, float)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``(y_min, y_max)``. When omitted it is auto-computed (5% padding, baseline ``0`` always included) from the tallest bar that can actually be drawn at *any* zoom — i.e. across the raw bars and every LOD level. This matters for ``aggregate='sum'``, whose wide-bin totals far exceed individual values: a raw-only range would clip the zoomed-out bars. For ``'mean'``/``'max'`` the aggregates stay within the raw range, so the result is unchanged.

<code>[**bin_width**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Width of each bar in base pairs at the finest zoom level. Auto-computed from the median spacing of ``x`` when omitted.

<code>[**stack**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, group contributions at each x-bin stack on top of each other (positive values above ``0``, negative below). Group order determines stacking order. When False (default), bars from different groups overlap, matching :meth:`add_segment_track`'s convention.

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, tuple thereof, or False]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``(256, 1024, 4096)``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Resolution levels for the multi-resolution LOD, matching the segment-track convention. Each entry is a bin *count* (``int``) or a physical bin *size* in base pairs (``str`` such as ``'5kb'``; units ``bp``/``kb``/``Mb``/``Gb``, bare number means bp); bp sizes become per-chromosome counts (``ceil(chrom_size / size)``, capped at 65536). Entries may be mixed, e.g. ``(256, 1024, '5kb')``. When zoomed out, the renderer picks the finest level whose bin maps to at least ~2 CSS pixels, keeping the visible bar count bounded by chromosome size. Pass ``False`` (or an empty tuple) to disable LOD and always render the original bars.

<code>[**aggregate**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'mean\', \'sum\', \'max\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'mean\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   How to combine multiple input bins that fall inside a single LOD bin. Only relevant when LOD is engaged.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{group}``, ``{value}``, ``{x}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated alias of ``zoom_windows``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``aggregate`` is not one of ``'mean'``, ``'sum'``, ``'max'``.

### add_line_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_line_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_line_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    x='pos',
    y='value',
    group_by=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    height=60,
    y_range=None,
    y_scale='linear',
    step=None,
    alpha=None,
    color=None,
    c=None,
    lw=None,
    linewidth=None,
    ls=None,
    linestyle=None,
    zoom_windows=(256, 1024, 4096),
    aggregate='mean',
    y_range_per_zoom=True,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
    density_windows=None,
    y_range_per_lod=None,
)
```

Add a line track — one connected polyline per group.

A missing ``y`` value (``NaN``) breaks the line, as in matplotlib:
the line stops at the last sample before it and resumes at the
next sample after it. Positions that simply have no row are
bridged, so add ``NaN`` rows where the line should break. When
zoomed out, a bin whose samples are all ``NaN`` is a gap; other
bins aggregate their non-``NaN`` samples.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, the column named by ``x``, the column named by ``y``, and any optional ``group_by`` column.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**x**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'pos\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for genomic position.

<code>[**y**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'value\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for the y-axis value.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose unique values become separate groups (each drawn as its own polyline).

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. Overridden by ``color``/``c`` when those are supplied.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [None, str, list, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Group palette, used when ``color_map`` is omitted. ``None`` uses the active matplotlib ``axes.prop_cycle``. Strings are resolved as colormap names first (``'viridis'``, ``'tab10'``, ...) then fall back to single-colour literals.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [60]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels.

<code>[**y_range**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of (float, float)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``(y_min, y_max)`` in data units, also on a log axis (where both must be positive). Auto-computed from data with 5% padding when omitted.

<code>[**y_scale**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'linear\', \'log\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'linear\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``'log'`` draws the y-axis on a base-10 log scale, ticked at powers of ten. Rows with ``y <= 0`` have no position on a log axis and are dropped with a :class:`UserWarning`. Zoomed-out levels aggregate the raw values (so ``aggregate='mean'`` is still the arithmetic mean) and place the result on the log axis. Tooltips report data values.

<code>[**step**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Step mode for a staircase line, matching matplotlib's ``step`` parameter. One of ``'pre'``, ``'post'``, ``'mid'``. ``None`` gives a straight-line interpolation between samples.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Opacity in ``[0, 1]`` applied to every group. Defaults to ``1.0``. If ``color`` carries an alpha channel and ``alpha`` is not given, that alpha is lifted out.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Any](`typing.Any`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Single matplotlib-style colour applied to all groups. Overrides ``color_map``. Examples: ``'C0'``, ``'red'``, ``'#ff8800'``, ``'#ff880040'``, ``(1, 0, 0, 0.5)``.

<code>[**c**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Any](`typing.Any`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Single matplotlib-style colour applied to all groups. Overrides ``color_map``. Examples: ``'C0'``, ``'red'``, ``'#ff8800'``, ``'#ff880040'``, ``(1, 0, 0, 0.5)``.

<code>[**lw**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Accepted only as ``None`` or ``1`` — WebGL2 fixes line width at 1 device pixel. Other values raise :class:`NotImplementedError`. For thicker bands use :meth:`add_fill_track`.

<code>[**linewidth**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Accepted only as ``None`` or ``1`` — WebGL2 fixes line width at 1 device pixel. Other values raise :class:`NotImplementedError`. For thicker bands use :meth:`add_fill_track`.

<code>[**ls**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Accepted only as ``None`` / ``'-'`` / ``'solid'``. Dashed and dotted lines raise :class:`NotImplementedError`.

<code>[**linestyle**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Accepted only as ``None`` / ``'-'`` / ``'solid'``. Dashed and dotted lines raise :class:`NotImplementedError`.

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, tuple thereof, or False]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``(256, 1024, 4096)``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Level-of-detail resolutions. Each entry is either a bin *count* (``int``) or a physical bin *size* (``str`` such as ``'10kb'``); a bp size is resolved to a count per chromosome. When zoomed out, the renderer draws the coarsest level whose bins still cover at least 2 CSS pixels and falls back to the raw samples once they are far enough apart. Pass ``False`` (or ``()``) to disable LOD and always ship only the raw samples.

<code>[**aggregate**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'mean\', \'sum\', \'max\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'mean\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   How samples sharing a bin are combined in the zoomed-out levels. With ``y_scale='log'`` the aggregate is taken over the data values before they are placed on the log axis.

<code>[**y_range_per_zoom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Emit a per-level ``(y_min, y_max)`` so the axis rescales when the renderer switches levels. Ignored when ``y_range`` is given explicitly.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{group}``, ``{value}``, ``{x}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``zoom_windows`` and ``y_range_per_zoom``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

<code>[**y_range_per_lod**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``zoom_windows`` and ``y_range_per_zoom``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[TypeError](`TypeError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If conflicting aliases are passed (e.g. both ``lw`` and ``linewidth``, or both ``color`` and ``c``).

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``alpha`` is outside ``[0, 1]``, ``step`` is not in ``{None, 'pre', 'post', 'mid'}``, or ``y_scale`` is not ``'linear'`` / ``'log'``; on a log axis, also if ``y_range`` is not positive or no ``y`` value is.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[NotImplementedError](`NotImplementedError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   For ``linewidth`` other than ``None`` / ``1`` or ``linestyle`` other than ``None`` / ``'-'`` / ``'solid'``.

### add_point_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_point_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_point_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    x='pos',
    y='value',
    group_by=None,
    value_col=None,
    n_bins=70,
    vmin=None,
    vmax=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    height=60,
    y_range=None,
    y_scale='linear',
    point_size=3,
    alpha=None,
    color=None,
    c=None,
    s=None,
    size=None,
    marker=None,
    zoom_windows=(256, 1024, 4096),
    aggregate='mean',
    y_range_per_zoom=True,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
    density_windows=None,
    y_range_per_lod=None,
)
```

Add a point track — point cloud rendered with ``gl.POINTS``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, the column named by ``x``, the column named by ``y``, and any optional ``group_by`` / ``value_col`` columns.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**x**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'pos\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for genomic position.

<code>[**y**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'value\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column for the y-axis value.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose unique values become separate groups (each drawn with its own colour). Mutually exclusive with ``value_col``.

<code>[**value_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column used to colour individual points. Non-numeric or low-cardinality values are treated as discrete categories (one colour per category). Numeric columns are binned into ``n_bins`` quantile buckets and coloured along the palette. Mutually exclusive with ``group_by``.

<code>[**n_bins**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [70]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Number of bins when ``value_col`` is continuous. Large defaults (≈10× categorical resolution) give a visually smooth colour ramp; pass a smaller value (e.g. 5–9) for a banded look or when a matching colorbar is in play.

<code>[**vmin**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Clamp the continuous range when binning ``value_col``. Auto-inferred from the data when omitted.

<code>[**vmax**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Clamp the continuous range when binning ``value_col``. Auto-inferred from the data when omitted.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. Overridden by ``color``/``c`` when those are supplied.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [None, str, list, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Group palette. ``None`` uses the active matplotlib ``axes.prop_cycle``. Strings are resolved as colormap names first (``'viridis'``, ``'tab10'``, ...) then fall back to single-colour literals. For ``value_col`` with a continuous column the default becomes ``'viridis'`` when ``palette`` is left as ``None``.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [60]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels.

<code>[**y_range**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of (float, float)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``(y_min, y_max)`` in data units, also on a log axis (where both must be positive). Auto-computed from data with 5% padding when omitted.

<code>[**y_scale**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'linear\', \'log\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'linear\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``'log'`` draws the y-axis on a base-10 log scale, ticked at powers of ten. Rows with ``y <= 0`` have no position on a log axis and are dropped with a :class:`UserWarning`. Zoomed-out levels aggregate the raw values (so ``aggregate='mean'`` is still the arithmetic mean) and place the result on the log axis. Tooltips report data values.

<code>[**point_size**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [3]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Point diameter in CSS pixels. Aliases: ``s`` / ``size``.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Opacity in ``[0, 1]`` applied to every group. Defaults to ``0.85`` (the prior visual). If ``color`` carries an alpha channel and ``alpha`` is not given, that alpha is lifted out.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Any](`typing.Any`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Single matplotlib-style colour applied to all points. Overrides ``color_map`` and ``value_col`` colouring.

<code>[**c**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Any](`typing.Any`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Single matplotlib-style colour applied to all points. Overrides ``color_map`` and ``value_col`` colouring.

<code>[**s**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Aliases for ``point_size``.

<code>[**size**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Aliases for ``point_size``.

<code>[**marker**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Accepted only as ``None`` / ``'.'`` / ``'s'`` (filled square, the only shape WebGL ``gl.POINTS`` produces). Other values raise :class:`NotImplementedError` rather than silently rendering a square.

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, tuple thereof, or False]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``(256, 1024, 4096)``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Level-of-detail resolutions. Each entry is either a bin *count* (``int``) or a physical bin *size* (``str`` such as ``'10kb'``); a bp size is resolved to a count per chromosome. When zoomed out, the renderer draws the coarsest level whose bins still cover at least 2 CSS pixels and falls back to the raw samples once they are far enough apart. Pass ``False`` (or ``()``) to disable LOD and always ship only the raw samples.

<code>[**aggregate**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'mean\', \'sum\', \'max\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'mean\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   How samples sharing a bin are combined in the zoomed-out levels. With ``y_scale='log'`` the aggregate is taken over the data values before they are placed on the log axis.

<code>[**y_range_per_zoom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Emit a per-level ``(y_min, y_max)`` so the axis rescales when the renderer switches levels. Ignored when ``y_range`` is given explicitly.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available keys: ``{group}``, ``{value}``, ``{x}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``zoom_windows`` and ``y_range_per_zoom``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

<code>[**y_range_per_lod**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated aliases of ``zoom_windows`` and ``y_range_per_zoom``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[TypeError](`TypeError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If conflicting aliases are passed, or if both ``group_by`` and ``value_col`` are supplied.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``alpha`` is outside ``[0, 1]``, ``n_bins < 1``, or ``y_scale`` is not ``'linear'`` / ``'log'``; on a log axis, also if ``y_range`` is not positive or no ``y`` value is.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[NotImplementedError](`NotImplementedError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``marker`` is anything other than ``None`` / ``'.'`` / ``'s'``.

### add_segment_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_segment_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_segment_track(
    df,
    name,
    *,
    start='start',
    end='end',
    group_by=None,
    individual_col=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    height=None,
    zoom_windows=(256, 1024, 4096),
    stack=False,
    tip_fmt=None,
    tip_label=None,
    density_windows=None,
)
```

Add a segment track rendered with GPU-instanced rectangles.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**df**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Long-format frame with columns ``chrom``, the interval start and end columns (see ``start`` / ``end``), and any of the optional ``group_by`` / ``individual_col`` columns referenced below.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Track display label shown in the left panel.

<code>[**start**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``, ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Columns holding each interval's start and end coordinates.

<code>[**end**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``, ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Columns holding each interval's start and end coordinates.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column whose unique values become separate sub-rows.

<code>[**individual_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column identifying individuals. When provided, each individual gets its own horizontal row within the group band (stacked haplotype view); track height auto-adapts so each row is at least 1 px.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: '#rrggbb'}``. When omitted, colours cycle through the built-in palette in group order.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [None, str, list, or matplotlib.colors.Colormap]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Group palette, used when ``color_map`` is omitted. ``None`` uses the active matplotlib ``axes.prop_cycle``. Strings are resolved as colormap names first (``'viridis'``, ``'tab10'``, ...) then fall back to single-colour literals.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track height in CSS pixels. Defaults to ``max(60, nrows)`` (matches the other plot tracks' default of 60, with an automatic bump when ``individual_col`` produces more rows), capped at 400 so a large ``group_by`` x ``individual_col`` grid doesn't render an absurdly tall track. Pass an explicit ``height`` for the full-resolution haplotype view (one visible pixel per row).

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, tuple thereof, or False]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``(256, 1024, 4096)``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Resolution levels for the multi-resolution density LOD. Each entry is either a bin *count* (``int``) or a physical bin *size* in base pairs (``str`` such as ``'5kb'``, ``'1.5Mb'``, ``'500'``; units ``bp``/``kb``/``Mb``/``Gb``, bare number means bp). bp sizes are converted to per-chromosome counts (``ceil(chrom_size / size)``), so the same string gives the same physical bin width on every chromosome. Counts are used as-is; bp-derived counts are capped at 65536. A single value is treated as one level; entries may be mixed, e.g. ``(256, 1024, '5kb')``. Pass ``False`` (or an empty tuple) to disable LOD and always draw the raw segments.

<code>[**stack**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, groups' density contributions stack on top of each other in the zoomed-out density view (rather than overlapping). Normalisation uses the combined max across all bins. Requires ``group_by`` with more than one group; ignored when ``individual_col`` is set.

<code>[**tip_fmt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Python format string for tooltips. Available key: ``{group}``.

<code>[**tip_label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Heading shown above the tooltip body. Defaults to ``f'{name}:'``.

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated alias of ``zoom_windows``. Passing one emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

### add_spans { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_spans }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_spans(
    ranges,
    chrom=None,
    *,
    start='start',
    end='end',
    group_by=None,
    color=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    alpha=0.1,
    edgecolor=None,
    edgewidth=0.0,
    dash=None,
    replace=False,
)
```

Add shaded vertical spans across all tracks.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**ranges**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [Iterable](`Iterable`)\[[tuple](`tuple`)\] \| [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Iterable](`Iterable`)\[[tuple](`tuple`)\]\] \| [pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``(start, end)`` pairs in base pairs, in any of three shapes:  - one pair, or an iterable of pairs, all on one chromosome; - a dict mapping chromosome name to an iterable of pairs   (``chrom`` is ignored in that case); - a DataFrame, reading the bounds from the columns named by   ``start`` and ``end`` and chromosomes as described under   ``chrom``. Rows with a missing bound are skipped.

<code>[**chrom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Chromosome for the spans; defaults to the current viewport chromosome. Ignored when ``ranges`` is a dict. When ``ranges`` is a DataFrame this may instead name the *column* holding each row's chromosome — a column of that name takes precedence over a chromosome of the same name — and when it is omitted a ``'chrom'`` column is used if the frame has one.

<code>[**start**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'`` / ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   DataFrame columns holding the span bounds. Ignored for the other input shapes.

<code>[**end**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'`` / ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   DataFrame columns holding the span bounds. Ignored for the other input shapes.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   DataFrame column whose distinct values each get their own colour, drawn from ``palette``. Requires DataFrame input, and is mutually exclusive with ``color`` — one flat colour would overwrite every group's. Rows with a missing group value fall back to the default colour.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: colour}`` overriding individual entries of the palette. Only meaningful alongside ``group_by``.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[optional](`optional`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Qualitative palette for the groups, resolved the same way as on the track methods. Only meaningful alongside ``group_by``.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Fill colour, default ``'#ffcc44'``.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``0.1``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Fill opacity in ``[0, 1]``.

<code>[**edgecolor**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Outline colour. Defaults to ``color`` if an ``edgewidth`` is given.

<code>[**edgewidth**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``0.0``]{.parameter-default}</code>

<code>[**dash**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of int]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Dash pattern for the outline, e.g. ``[4, 3]``.

<code>[**replace**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``False``]{.parameter-default}</code>
