### add_ucsc_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_ucsc_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_ucsc_track(
    ucsc_track=None,
    name=None,
    *,
    kind='line',
    assembly=None,
    chrom=None,
    start=None,
    end=None,
    x='start',
    step=_UCSC_STEP_DEFAULT,
    color=None,
    start_col='start',
    end_col='end',
    zoom_windows=None,
    density_windows=None,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Fetch a UCSC track and add it as a widget track of the given kind.

Thin wrapper around :func:`geneinfo.ucsc.get_track` that forwards
the fetched DataFrame to :meth:`add_point_track`,
:meth:`add_line_track`, :meth:`add_histogram_track`,
:meth:`add_fill_track`, :meth:`add_segment_track` or
:meth:`add_heatmap_track` depending on ``kind``. For the
quantitative kinds the adapter auto-detects which source column
holds the numeric signal and renames it to ``'value'``, so the
user never needs to know the track's native schema. The interval
kinds (``'segment'``, ``'heatmap'``) draw each record's
``start``-``end`` span and need no numeric column.

If the auto-detected column is wrong for your purposes, fetch
the track yourself and pass the DataFrame to the underlying
``add_*`` method::

    from geneinfo.ucsc import get_track
    df = get_track('trackName', 'hg38',
                   chrom='chr1', start=..., end=...,
                   value_column='pValue')
    Tracks('hg38').add_line_track(df, 'My track', x='start', y='value')

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**ucsc_track**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   UCSC track identifier (see :func:`geneinfo.ucsc.search_tracks`). The legacy keyword ``track_name=`` is accepted for one release with a deprecation warning.

<code>[**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Track display label. Defaults to ``ucsc_track``.

<code>[**kind**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'point\', \'line\', \'histogram\', \'fill\', \'segment\', \'heatmap\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'point\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Which widget track to draw. ``'point'`` maps to :meth:`add_point_track`, ``'segment'`` to :meth:`add_segment_track` and ``'heatmap'`` to :meth:`add_heatmap_track`. A heatmap draws the whole track as a single row unless ``individual_col=`` is passed, and shades each cell by the number of records overlapping it (``shade='count'``, scaled to the busiest cell; pass ``shade='log_count'`` for a log scale, or ``value_col=`` to colour by a column instead).

<code>[**assembly**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Genome assembly. Inherits from ``Tracks(assembly)`` when omitted.

<code>[**chrom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Optional region restriction passed to the UCSC API. When omitted, the track is fetched genome-wide (or for the current viewport's chromosome, if set). These are coordinates, not column names; see ``start_col`` / ``end_col`` for those.

<code>[**start**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Optional region restriction passed to the UCSC API. When omitted, the track is fetched genome-wide (or for the current viewport's chromosome, if set). These are coordinates, not column names; see ``start_col`` / ``end_col`` for those.

<code>[**end**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Optional region restriction passed to the UCSC API. When omitted, the track is fetched genome-wide (or for the current viewport's chromosome, if set). These are coordinates, not column names; see ``start_col`` / ``end_col`` for those.

<code>[**x**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Column to use as the x position for the quantitative kinds. Pass ``'mid'`` to use the interval midpoint. Not used by ``'segment'`` / ``'heatmap'``.

<code>[**step**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) or None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [_UCSC_STEP_DEFAULT]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Step mode for ``kind='line'`` or ``kind='fill'`` (one of ``'pre'``, ``'post'``, ``'mid'``, or ``None``). Defaults to ``'post'`` when ``x='start'`` and ``None`` when ``x='mid'`` (there's no interval extent to step across when plotting at midpoints). Ignored for ``kind='point'`` and ``kind='histogram'``; not accepted for ``'segment'`` / ``'heatmap'``.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[optional](`optional`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Single colour applied to the track. For ``kind='point'`` and ``kind='line'`` it is forwarded as ``color=``; for the other kinds it is translated into the ``color_map`` those methods expect, applied to every group.

<code>[**start_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``, ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Columns of the fetched table holding the interval bounds drawn by ``kind='segment'`` / ``'heatmap'`` (forwarded as their ``start`` / ``end``). The fetched table already names UCSC's ``chromStart`` / ``chromEnd`` ``start`` / ``end``, so change these only to draw other bounds, e.g. ``start_col='thickStart', end_col='thickEnd'``. Not used by the quantitative kinds.

<code>[**end_col**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'start\'``, ``\'end\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Columns of the fetched table holding the interval bounds drawn by ``kind='segment'`` / ``'heatmap'`` (forwarded as their ``start`` / ``end``). The fetched table already names UCSC's ``chromStart`` / ``chromEnd`` ``start`` / ``end``, so change these only to draw other bounds, e.g. ``start_col='thickStart', end_col='thickEnd'``. Not used by the quantitative kinds.

<code>[**zoom_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int, str, tuple thereof, or False]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Level-of-detail resolutions, forwarded to the underlying ``add_*`` method. ``None`` (the default) keeps that method's own default: ``(256, 1024, 4096)`` for every kind except ``'heatmap'``, whose default is ``1000``. Each entry is a bin count (``int``) or a bin size (``str`` such as ``'10kb'``). Pass ``False`` or ``()`` to disable LOD and always ship every sample (not supported by ``'heatmap'``).

<code>[**density_windows**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`) \| [int](`int`) \| [str](`str`) \| None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Deprecated alias of ``zoom_windows``. Passing it emits a ``DeprecationWarning``.

<code>[****kwargs**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Any](`typing.Any`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [{}]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Forwarded to the underlying ``add_*`` call, e.g. ``y_scale='log'`` for ``kind='point'`` or ``kind='line'``, or ``group_by='svType'`` for ``kind='segment'``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, for chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``kind`` is not one of the supported values, if no assembly is resolvable, if a quantitative kind is requested for a track with no numeric column the adapter could expose as ``value``, or if ``start_col`` / ``end_col`` are combined with a quantitative kind.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[TypeError](`TypeError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``x`` or ``step`` is passed with ``kind='segment'`` / ``'heatmap'``.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``start_col`` / ``end_col`` name columns the fetched table does not have.

### add_vlines { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_vlines }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.add_vlines(
    positions,
    chrom=None,
    *,
    pos='pos',
    group_by=None,
    color=None,
    color_map=None,
    palette=None,
    linewidth=1.0,
    alpha=0.3,
    dash=None,
    replace=False,
)
```

Add thin vertical guide lines across all tracks.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**positions**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`) \| [Iterable](`Iterable`)\[[int](`int`)\] \| [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Iterable](`Iterable`)\[[int](`int`)\]\] \| [pandas](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Base-pair positions, in any of three shapes:  - a number, or an iterable of numbers, all on one chromosome; - a dict mapping chromosome name to an iterable of positions   (``chrom`` is ignored in that case); - a DataFrame, reading positions from the column named by   ``pos`` and chromosomes as described under ``chrom``. Rows   with a missing position are skipped.

<code>[**chrom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Chromosome for the positions; defaults to the current viewport chromosome. Ignored when ``positions`` is a dict. When ``positions`` is a DataFrame this may instead name the *column* holding each row's chromosome — a column of that name takes precedence over a chromosome of the same name — and when it is omitted a ``'chrom'`` column is used if the frame has one.

<code>[**pos**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``\'pos\'``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   DataFrame column holding the positions. Ignored for the other input shapes.

<code>[**group_by**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   DataFrame column whose distinct values each get their own colour, drawn from ``palette``. Requires DataFrame input, and is mutually exclusive with ``color`` — one flat colour would overwrite every group's. Rows with a missing group value fall back to the default colour.

<code>[**color_map**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   ``{group_value: colour}`` overriding individual entries of the palette. Only meaningful alongside ``group_by``.

<code>[**palette**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[optional](`optional`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Qualitative palette for the groups, resolved the same way as on the track methods. Only meaningful alongside ``group_by``.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Matplotlib-style colour spec; resolved through :func:`_resolve_color_mapping` so names like ``'C0'`` or ``'red'`` work. When omitted (``None``), the guides follow the active theme's text colour — white on a dark theme, black on a light one — so they stay legible on either background.

<code>[**linewidth**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``1.0``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Line width in CSS pixels.

<code>[**alpha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``0.3``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Opacity in ``[0, 1]``. Values outside the range are clamped.

<code>[**dash**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of int]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Canvas dash pattern, e.g. ``[4, 3]``. ``None`` = solid.

<code>[**replace**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``False``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, replace existing vlines. Otherwise append.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[TypeError](`TypeError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``group_by`` is combined with ``color``, if ``group_by`` is given without DataFrame input, or if ``positions`` is a ``str``.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If a named column is absent from the DataFrame.

### colorbar { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.colorbar }

```python

    track_name,
    *,

    orientation='horizontal',

```

Build a compact matplotlib key for a value-mode heatmap.

Continuous tracks render as a small colorbar; discrete tracks
as a stacked swatch/label legend. Density-mode tracks have no
palette and raise :class:`ValueError`.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

:   Name of a heatmap track added via :meth:`add_heatmap_track`.

<code>[**ax**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[matplotlib](`matplotlib`).[axes](`matplotlib.axes`).[Axes](`matplotlib.axes.Axes`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Target axes. When omitted, a small figure is created at ``figsize`` (small by default — ~30% of the legacy size).

<code>[**orientation**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'horizontal\', \'vertical\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'horizontal\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Colorbar orientation (continuous mode only).

<code>[**label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Title / axis label. Defaults to the track's ``value_col``.

<code>[**figsize**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [([float](`float`), [float](`float`))]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Figure size in inches. Defaults to ``(1.25, 0.22)`` for horizontal continuous / discrete, ``(0.22, 1.25)`` for vertical continuous.

<code>[**dpi**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Figure DPI; matplotlib default when omitted.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[matplotlib](`matplotlib`).[figure](`matplotlib.figure`).[Figure](`matplotlib.figure.Figure`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The figure containing the key.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If no heatmap track is named ``track_name``.

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

### hide_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.hide_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.hide_track(name_or_index)
```

Hide tracks without removing them.

A name hides every track with that name; an index hides the one
track at that position. The track disappears from the view, but its data stays in the
widget (in Python and in the browser), so :meth:`show_track`
brings it back instantly, in its original position, without
re-sending or re-building anything. Hiding a hidden track does
nothing.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**name_or_index**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) or [int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The track's display ``name``, or a positional index into :attr:`track_configs` (negative indices count from the end). Hidden tracks keep their position, so they count too.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, for fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If no track matches.

#### See Also {.doc-section .doc-section-see-also}

show_track, remove_track

### legend { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.legend }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.legend(
    *track_names,
    orientation='horizontal',
    align='right',
    gap=0.1,
    figsize=None,
    dpi=None,
    labels=None,
)
```

Arm a legend strip to appear above the widget on display.

Records which value-mode heatmap tracks to summarise and how to
lay them out. The legend is *not* rendered until the widget
itself is displayed (i.e. when ``self`` is a cell's last
expression, or ``display(self)`` is called). Returns ``self`` so
the call chains naturally:

>>> v.add_heatmap_track(...).add_heatmap_track(...)
>>> v.legend('Score', 'Ancestry')   # arms, returns v
>>> v                               # renders widget + legend

Validation happens up-front: unknown names raise :class:`KeyError`
and density-mode tracks raise :class:`ValueError`.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[***track_names**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [()]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Names of value-mode heatmap tracks, in left-to-right order.

<code>[**orientation**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'horizontal\', \'vertical\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'horizontal\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Colorbar orientation for continuous keys.

<code>[**align**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'right\', \'center\', \'left\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'right\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Horizontal alignment against the notebook cell.

<code>[**gap**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [``0.10``]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Inches between adjacent keys.

<code>[**figsize**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [([float](`float`), [float](`float`))]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Figure size in inches. Auto-sized to content when omitted.

<code>[**dpi**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Figure DPI.

<code>[**labels**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Per-track title override, e.g. ``{'Score': 'selection'}``. Missing entries fall back to the track's ``value_col``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, for fluent chaining.

### select_tracks { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.select_tracks }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.select_tracks(names)
```

Show only the listed tracks, in the order listed.

A shortcut for hiding every track, then showing the listed ones,
except that the shown tracks are also reordered to follow
``names``. The remaining tracks stay hidden, after the shown ones
and in their existing order, so their data is kept and a later
:meth:`show_track` or :meth:`select_tracks` restores them
instantly.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**names**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [str, int, or iterable of str or int]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Tracks to show. Each entry is a display name, which selects every track with that name (in their existing order), or a positional index into :attr:`track_configs` as it is before the call. A track listed twice is placed at its first mention. An empty list hides every track.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, for fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If any entry matches no track. The viewer is left unchanged.

#### See Also {.doc-section .doc-section-see-also}

added_tracks, hide_track, show_track

### set_viewport { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.set_viewport }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.set_viewport(chrom, start, end)
```

Move the viewport to a new chromosome and base-pair window.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**chrom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Chromosome name (must exist in the widget's ``chrom_sizes``).

<code>[**start**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Inclusive start position in base pairs. Negative values are clamped to ``0``.

<code>[**end**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Exclusive end position in base pairs. Values past the end of the chromosome are clamped to its length.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If ``chrom`` is not in :attr:`chrom_sizes`.

### show_track { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.show_track }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.show_track(name_or_index)
```

Show tracks hidden with :meth:`hide_track`.

A name shows every track with that name; an index shows the one
track at that position. The track reappears in the position it had before it was
hidden. Showing a visible track does nothing.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**name_or_index**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) or [int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The track's display ``name``, or a positional index into :attr:`track_configs` (negative indices count from the end).

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, for fluent chaining.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[KeyError](`KeyError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If no track matches.

#### See Also {.doc-section .doc-section-see-also}

hide_track

### zoom_to { #geneinfo.widget.Tracks.zoom_to }

```python
geneinfo.widget.Tracks.zoom_to(
    chrom,
    start=None,
    end=None,
    *,
    center=None,
    window=None,
)
```

Zoom the viewport to a chromosome, range, or centred window.

Supports three calling styles:

* ``zoom_to('chrX')`` — show the whole chromosome.
* ``zoom_to('chrX', start=100_000, end=200_000)`` — show the
  given half-open range ``[start, end)``. ``start`` and
  ``end`` may also be passed positionally.
* ``zoom_to('chrX', center=150_000, window=1_000_000)`` —
  centre on ``center`` with the given window width. ``window``
  defaults to ``1_000_000`` bp when omitted.

The ``start``/``end`` and ``center``/``window`` styles are
mutually exclusive.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**chrom**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Chromosome name.

<code>[**start**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Inclusive start position in base pairs. When given, ``end`` must also be given (and ``center``/``window`` must not).

<code>[**end**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Exclusive end position in base pairs.

<code>[**center**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Genomic position to centre on, in base pairs. Keyword-only.

<code>[**window**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Total window width in base pairs. Keyword-only. Defaults to ``1_000_000`` when ``center`` is given. The viewport is set to ``[center - window // 2, center + window // 2)`` then clamped to the chromosome bounds by :meth:`set_viewport`.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Tracks](`geneinfo.widget.segment_viewer_gl.Tracks`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   ``self``, to support fluent chaining.
